expiry_mechanism: Native validity scanner disables assignment; native unassign action filters exact PAM role and disabled status, then recomputes/reconciles the same user

approval.execution: Automated tests of distinct identities; no human review timing claimed
approval.requester: Authorized setup administrator; standard user self-service was not tested

windows.active: Same identity; UAC consent and elevated read query succeeded
windows.expired_existing_process: Read query not tested: console auto-locked; actual quser observation showed the Windows session remained Active after AD revocation
windows.expired_fresh_signin: Sign-out alone retained stale group information. After client restart and online sign-in, query denied and Administrators SID absent (native findstr exit1)
windows.clock_qualification: Initial client clock was three hours ahead and timezone Pacific; client domain time synchronization corrected before final fresh sign-in. Capture provenance and membership timeline use aligned reference clocks.

restart_recovery.scope: Existing application restart during active access; no outage across expiry or host reboot tested

prior_failed_trial.correction: Replaced recompute-only task with supported native disabled-assignment unassign and reconciliation; shared mapping restored

limitations: Configured validity is not exact enforcement time
Approval consumes part of the fixed validity window
Membership revocation does not terminate existing Windows tokens
Windows sign-out alone retained stale groups; final test required a client restart
Old elevated-process read query was not tested because console auto-locked
Full independent manual replay not performed
Outage spanning expiry and host reboot recovery not tested
